answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect punishment matrices ensure Sybil resistance by creating a formidable capital barrier where each identity must continuously bid, in an ocean of strategic adversaries, its own expected future value. In Nash equilibrium, any attempt to multiply identities, hollowing out genuine engagement, results in a negative payoff, akin to the relentless advance of a glacier eroding terrain, ensuring that rational players converge to a single, authentic identity.
